text:
Maria: Quick workshop recap + proposal: scoped observability pilot we discussed today. Objective: deliver a small Console surface for per-route cost + error analytics MVP, plus tracing hooks + a safe sampling policy. Pilot targets: internal org + 1 external (Acme).

Kevin: Sounds good. Two main runtime asks: deterministic full traces for a few hot routes, and a lightweight global sampler elsewhere. We should make hot-route list editable per-org.

Anya: Ops constraints: exporters must not block request latency. We'll implement an async exporter queue with bounded capacity and drop-on-overflow. Also need an automated kill-switch if trace export error rate spikes.

Phil: Cost sketch: assuming 500k req/day and 3% full traces -> ~40GB/week of full trace storage. Rough infra cost $900/mo for that customer. I'll add a small worksheet for Acme with both 3% and 10% scenarios.

Lina: UI MVP (minimal): 1) Per-route cost card (top 10 routes) with daily delta and % spend, 2) Error analytics table (fingerprint, count, % traffic, first/last seen), 3) Link to trace viewer from each error row. No heavy exploration or custom dashboards in MVP.

Jake: For tracing hooks, propose a JSON policy editor + presets. Example policy: ```json
{"hot_routes":["/v1/chat","/v1/generate"],"hot_full_pct":100,"global_sample_pct":0.5,"reservoir_per_min":30}
```
We'll keep feature flags so we can flip per-org during canary.

Maria: Proposed acceptance criteria: - Per-route cost card in Console (top-10, daily/weekly) - Error analytics MVP (fingerprinting + trace link) - Tracing policy UI with hot-route override and a simple JSON preset - Canary: internal 48h -> Acme 7d pilot - Safety SLO: enabling sampling must not increase request p95 by >2% and exporter queue latency <200ms.

Kevin: Implementation notes: runtime will tag traces with org_id + route for aggregation. We need lightweight span summaries for cost estimates (span meta only) to avoid storing full payloads unless sampled. Also add metric emission: traced_requests_count, traced_bytes, exporter_queue_depth.

Anya: Canary gating checklist: 1) trace_export_errors < 0.1% 2) exporter_queue_depth < 1000 3) end-to-end trace latency < 300ms. If any fail, auto-roll back sampling for the org.

Phil: Deliverables: cost worksheet for Acme + global sensitivity (3/5/10% full traces), expected infra delta, and a recommended billing signal (per-tenant trace bytes). I'll have a first pass by Thursday.

Lina: UX deliverables: mockups for the 3 widgets, copy for onboarding tooltip explaining sampling tradeoffs, and a quick admin flow to toggle hot-route overrides. ETA: Friday AM.

Maria: Owners + deadlines: Kevin (runtime + canary runbook) EOD Fri, Anya (ops gating + rollback) EOD Fri, Phil (cost model) Thu, Lina (UI mocks) Fri AM. I'll coordinate Acme onboarding and provide a synthetic dataset.

Kevin: I'll include an A/B variant in the canary: full traces for top-3 vs top-5 routes so we can measure diagnostic uplift vs cost. Also will add logs for exporter backpressure events.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary -> org:redwood-internal, start: 2025-06-02T09:00Z, duration: 48h.

Maria: One open question: retention tiers. My vote: 7d full traces, 30d span summaries, 90d error fingerprints. We can iterate. Anyone strongly opposed?

Phil: That retention mix matches the cost model for pilot customers. Long term we should expose retention as a billing tier.

Anya: Agree. Ops will add retention guardrails to the runbook so customers can't accidentally blow up costs.

Lina: UX: we'll hide retention controls in the admin area for now, surface defaults on onboarding.

Maria: OK, decision: proceed with the proposed scope and pilot plan. Action items recorded above. If no objections, I'll send stakeholder note and a calendar invite for canary kick-off. :rocket:
